core.subtitle: Core workflow
core.title: How does the Xiaohongshu account analyzer work?
core.description: MediaClaw connects four modules that find candidates, prepare evidence, run the analysis, and preserve the report—it is more than a profile viewer.

items.title: 1. Find benchmark Xiaohongshu creators from proven posts
items.description: Search a niche term and MediaClaw organizes strong posts and recurring authors, then adds public profile details, representative work, recommendation rationale, and low-follower/high-engagement signals. Use the shortlist to decide who deserves deeper review.

image.alt: MediaClaw benchmark account results with candidate creators, representative Xiaohongshu posts, and recommendation rationale

items.title: 2. Collect profile posts and start account analysis
items.description: Open a target creator profile and collect at least 50 public posts. The creator card keeps available profile, follower, and engagement fields, and the existing dataset can start the breakdown without rebuilding your research from scratch.

image.alt: Starting a Xiaohongshu account breakdown from an already collected creator profile in MediaClaw

items.title: 3. Stratify the sample, with manual control
items.description: The system selects high-engagement, representative, and comparison posts from the collected set. Review and adjust the sample before analysis so irrelevant content does not dilute the findings.

items.title: 4. Run in the background and keep every report

report.subtitle: Inside the report
report.title: What is inside a Xiaohongshu account analysis report?
report.description: A real report moves from positioning and topics through headlines, visuals, and voice, then produces ideas ready to pursue. The same evidence-led structure supports both Xiaohongshu creator analysis and Xiaohongshu competitor analysis.

items.title: Positioning and topic map
items.description: Define the audience, core value, and content boundaries first, then group representative posts by problem, scenario, audience, or recurring series. Evidence helps separate durable directions from one-off hits.

image.alt: MediaClaw account breakdown report showing the core account definition, topic map, and source materials

items.title: Headline and opening patterns
items.description: Compare the headline structures, keywords, emotional tension, and openings repeated across strong posts. The report turns those patterns into reusable principles instead of copying individual titles.

image.alt: MediaClaw account breakdown report showing headline patterns and representative title samples

items.title: Cover and visual system
items.description: Analyze cover composition, the main subject, text hierarchy, color, and information density, then connect those choices to representative posts and the account's recognizable visual identity.

image.alt: MediaClaw account breakdown report showing the cover visual system and representative posts

items.title: Voice and interaction language
items.description: Summarize recurring tone, sentence patterns, narrative rhythm, and interaction prompts, including how the creator builds trust, opens information gaps, and invites continued reading or discussion.

items.title: Writable ideas with source evidence

boundaries.subtitle: Data boundaries
boundaries.title: What are the data boundaries for RedNote profile analysis?
boundaries.description: A Xiaohongshu account analyzer should improve content research with public, traceable evidence—not access private data or make unsupported conclusions about a creator.

items.title: Public pages only
items.description: The workflow does not provide private accounts, creator dashboards, contact details, or information the platform does not make public.

items.title: Separate facts from inference
items.description: Profile fields and engagement counts are evidence. Positioning and content patterns are research conclusions that should be tested across more samples.

items.title: Use data responsibly
items.description: Use collected information only for authorized research, operations, and content review while following platform rules and applicable laws.

items.question: What is the difference between profile scraping and account analysis?
items.answer: Profile scraping organizes public account information and historical posts into a usable sample. Account analysis uses that evidence to examine positioning, recurring themes, publishing patterns, and engagement signals. Collection prepares the data; analysis structures the research.

items.question: How do I find the right competitor accounts to analyze?
items.answer: Start with keywords and content themes closest to your business. Notice which creators repeatedly appear in useful results, then filter by audience, category, format, and account stage rather than choosing only the biggest profiles.

items.question: How many posts do I need for an account analysis?
items.answer: Start by collecting at least 50 public posts from the target profile. The system selects high-engagement, representative, and comparison samples, and you can adjust the selection before analysis. A tiny sample can make one unusual post look like a stable strategy.

items.question: Do I need enhanced collection before starting an account breakdown?
items.answer: You can collect the initial profile-post set without enhanced collection. After you start the breakdown, the workflow enriches selected representative posts with the details and transcripts needed for analysis.

items.question: How long does a full account analysis take?
items.answer: A first complete analysis typically takes about 10-20 minutes, depending on sample size and how much evidence needs enrichment. The task can continue in the background, and the progress panel shows the current step.

items.question: Can this show an account's private audience demographics?
items.answer: No. This page does not provide creator-dashboard demographics. Public profiles, themes, and comments can suggest audience signals, but those are research inferences—not exact audience statistics.

items.question: What should I do after finishing an account analysis?
items.answer: Add priority creators to monitoring, save representative posts to your research library, and validate demand through comments and keywords. This turns a one-time report into an ongoing topic, creation, and review workflow.
